item.title: Bayern star leaves France camp following Italy defeat
item.description: Bayern star leaves France camp following Italy defeat Bayern Munich centre-back Dayot Upamecano has departed the French national team camp. The French Football Federation confirmed on Friday that the 28-year-old has left the camp early for personal reasons. Upamecano played the full game as France suffered a 3-1 defeat to Italy in the UEFA Nations League on Thursday, despite taking an early lead through Michael Olise. The Bayern defender conceded the penalty that allowed Pio Esposito to put Italy 3-1 ahead in the 74th minute. France coach Zinedine Zidane has initially decided against calling up a replacement for Upamecano. Les Bleus face Turkey in their final Group A1 fixture on Sunday.

item.title: ‘You’re disgusting’ – Fans hit out at Kyle Kuzma’s latest ‘free Palestine’ message
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Milwaukee Bucks star Kyle Kuzma has angered NBA fans with his latest take on Palestine. After parting ways with Giannis Antetokounmpo in the offseason, the Milwaukee Bucks are struggling to win games this season. Following their most recent defeat against the Los Angeles Lakers, the Bucks have slipped to the 15th spot in the Eastern Conference, with a league-worst 1-11 record. Even then, Bucks star Kyle Kuzma is apparently more worried about what’s happening in Palestine than about playing basketball. NBA fans sound off on Kyle Kuzma’s ‘Free Palestine’ demand In light of the Israel-Palestine conflict’s latest tragedy in Gaza, Kuzma prayed for the souls of citizens who passed away and demanded to ‘Free Palestine’ on X. “Praying for the lost souls at Nasser Hospital. Doctors and children dying in hospitals that are much needed in the region that are used as command centers for Hamas. Truly evil. Free Palestine,” Kuzma wrote on X . Kuzma’s message went viral and at the time of writing, already has over 1.9 million views on X. Despite that, most fans showed no sympathy to the Bucks star and instead demanded him to focus on his NBA career. “You’re disgusting,” a fan wrote. While another added, “You’re so disgusting please do not ever speak about my country again and focus on shooting over 30% from three before you end up playing in China.” “One of the few people who should actually shut up and dribble,” a third fan pointed out. A fourth fan stated, “Keep Palestine out of your propaganda prayers.” “What little respect there was for you left in the world just vanished just like that,” a furious fan claimed. So far, Kuzma is averaging 10.8 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game this season, but his off-court stance has continuously made fans angry. item.title: India's lowest ODI totals: Listing down Men in Blue's worst-ever performances in One-day cricket
item.description: India's lowest ODI totals: Listing down Men in Blue's worst-ever performances in One-day cricket originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India’s batting has suffered painful collapses on tours of New Zealand over the decades. India’s all-time lowest ODI total is far smaller than many fans might expect. A full list across all Test nations shows just how rare such collapses are. What is India's lowest score in ODI cricket? Full list of Men in Blue's worst totals India’s lowest ODI totals make for uncomfortable reading, even for a side that has won two World Cups and built a reputation for some of the most fearless batting in white-ball cricket. Every team has its bad days, but the scorecards below show that India’s worst afternoons came in a few clear patterns, most often against the swinging ball and on pitches that offered the bowlers more than they could handle. New Zealand has been one of the toughest places for those collapses to happen. India’s lowest ODI total on New Zealand soil is 92, a score recorded at Seddon Park in Hamilton on January 31, 2019, when the visitors were bowled out in 30.5 overs. Trent Boult was the destroyer that day with figures of 5 for 21, and Rohit Sharma, who was leading the side in his 200th ODI, could only watch as the innings fell apart. However, that Hamilton collapse wasn’t the first time the team had struggled badly in New Zealand. The 2002-03 tour remains the darkest period, as four of India’s five lowest totals in the country came on that single trip, and the hosts won the seven-match series 5-2. Two innings ended on 108, and two more finished on 122, which is why that tour is still remembered with a shudder. Across all countries, India have been bowled out for fewer than 100 on seven occasions, and the lowest of them all is 54 against Sri Lanka in Sharjah in 2000. MORE: Bavuma reveals why R Ashwin is the hardest bowler he has ever faced India’s lowest ODI totals in New Zealand The table below lists India’s ten lowest ODI totals in New Zealand, and the Hamilton 92 sits at the top. Four of the entries come from the 2002-03 tour, including the 108 at Eden Park in Auckland in the opening match, where New Zealand won by three wickets. The 108 at Christchurch on January 1, 2003 followed, and the two 122s came at Queenstown and Hamilton. The older entries show how long the problem goes back. The 138 at Dunedin in March 1990 was India’s opening match in a triangular series, and the 154 and 156 totals from February 1976 came in the first ODIs the two teams ever played in New Zealand. Those games were played with eight-ball overs, which is why the overs column shows “8-ball” for them. India lost the first one by nine wickets and the second by 80 runs. The 153 at Hamilton in February 1981 left India well short of a New Zealand total of 210, and the 149 at Auckland in March 2009 came in a series that India still won 3-1. item.title: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
item.description: Pat Cummins spent over an hour fielding questions over sandpapergate on Friday [Getty Images] As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," one woman watching the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Josh says he was surprised the scandal is back in the news [BBC] Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. There's a sense of injustice that Australia can't escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja has said he owed it to the three players punished to tell his side of the story [Getty Images] Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. David Warner, who received the most severe punishment of the Cape Town trio, said Khawaja was telling the truth and that Cummins' press conference denying the claims "threw him under the bus". Steve

item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous
item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. item.description: Atletico Madrid v FC Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/2027 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona midfielder Gavi has no intention of leaving the Catalan giants despite attracting transfer interest from European heavyweights Bayern Munich and Napoli. Midfielder rules out Camp Nou exit Reports from Marca reveal that the idea of departing Catalonia has never "crossed the player's mind", while sporting director Deco has zero desire to sanction a sale. Both the 22-year-old's camp and club hierarchy insist his future is completely secure despite recent enquiries from Italy and Germany. Having made 175 senior appearances since joining La Masia from Real Betis in 2015, the academy graduate wants to stay put. Fierce competition limits starting opportunities Gavi has been restricted to just 229 minutes across nine appearances this term - comprising five La Liga outings and four in the Champions League - with only two of those coming as a starter. Head coach Hansi Flick currently favours a first-choice double pivot of Pedri and Rodri, while youngster Marc Bernal has served as the primary deputy whenever either is unavailable, including during last weekend's victory away at Atletico Madrid. Pathways further forward are similarly congested for the versatile Andalusian. Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo currently share the attacking midfield duties, while Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi rotate on the left flank. Strong bond underpins mutual confidence Even though the Spanish publication notes that the midfielder is "not happy with his role", his motivation remains high and he stays "confident" of earning more minutes as the campaign progresses. Gavi even views the German tactician as a father figure, a bond highlighted when the pair shared a warm embrace on the touchline after sealing victory at the Metropolitano last weekend . Demanding winter schedule promises rotation With Barcelona facing a packed and demanding fixture list after the November international break, Flick is expected to rotate his squad far more frequently over the coming months. The driver wasted no time in sharing his thoughts on the new ride. “This is a tremendous opportunity to join MHR and compete full time again at a high level”, Sanchez said, according to Motorsport.com . item.title: Russia threatens hosts Germany if banned from men's ice hockey worlds
item.description: FILE PHOTO - The players of the USA (L) and Canada warm up before the start of the men's ice hockey match between Canada and USA during the 2026 Olympic Winter Games Milan Cortina. Ice hockey games at the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps could be moved to Paris or Lyon because the new mayor of Nice opposes a temporary venue in the home stadium of a local football club. (is associated with: «Russia threatens hosts Germany if banned from men's ice hockey worlds») Peter Kneffel/dpa Russia's ice hockey federation has threatened host nation Germany with compensation claims should it be banned from the men's 2027 world championships. A corresponding application has already been submitted to the ethics committee of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Russian federation president Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency. This comes amid the heated debate surrounding the reinstatement of Russia to international competition by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and the subsequent threat of boycott of the tournament from several nations and also sponsors. Canada, host of the men's world junior ice hockey championships at the end of the year, announced it will not grant visas to Russian players. In Germany, the federal government declared that hosting the tournament would be "virtually impossible" if Russia participated. "Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Tretiak said after a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and other sports officials. Several countries, including world champions Finland, have stated they will not compete against Russian teams. The Finnish and the Norwegian governments also announced this week that they will not issue visas to Russian athletes. The restrictions will initially have the greatest impact on winter sports, with a number of competitions taking place in Finland and Norway.

item.title: Could AI help decide medals at LA28 Olympics?
item.description: Gymnastics is leading the way in applying artificial intelligence to the judging of elite sport, and it could be used to help decide medals at the LA Olympics. Bosses in the sport said they would be "highly surprised" if AI-assisted judging was not implemented at the Games in 2028. This is despite some leading gymnasts criticising its use at the recent World Championships, saying they were "not robots" and warning it could be "dangerous". Olympic champion Carlos Yulo and British gymnast Harry Hepworth had the difficulty rating of their vaults downgraded in qualifying. Both were performing the piked Dragulescu and had their scores reduced from a 5.6 to a 5.2. They attempted the same vault in the final with Hepworth finishing sixth, while Yulo fell and came seventh. On his return from Rotterdam, Hepworth told BBC Sport: "On the half twist I bend my legs so that I can prepare for the landing, which I think is the most sensible thing to do because you don't want to break your legs or anything. "But the AI detection system caught on to it and said I was doing a tuck position, which then downgrades the vault by four tenths. "It definitely cost me a few positions, I think, in the final for sure." Referencing Yulo's experience, he said: "I think it does say a lot when me, the Olympic bronze medallist on vault, and the Olympic champion on vault are getting done by the AI system for the exact same thing. "In the final he really did go for the straight legs and it just made him fall because it's just really hard to do, and I think quite dangerous as well." Yulo said he was disappointed with the downgrading. "I don't know what the problem is," he told Inside Gymnastics. "It's AI, I'm not a robot, we're human beings, in my eyes and in my opinion. I think everyone also is maybe a bit disappointed about it because everyone is feeling it is pike position, why is it only 5.2?" Andrew Tombs, president of the Men's Artistic Gymnastics technical committee, believes the AI system can guarantee fairness for athletes and that is what they deserve. He said judges at the World Championships would have downgraded the difficulty rating - even without using the Judging Support System (JSS). But he did acknowledge lessons had been learned and that conversations were ongoing with coaches about the point at which the JSS should take its measurements. "I think the decisions made at the championships were correct based on what was in the system," he added. How does AI-assisted judging work? item.description: 2030 World Cup final a red line for Spain, according to Cadena SER The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has made its position clear to FIFA on the allocation of matches for the upcoming 2030 World Cup. According to Cadena SER 's El Larguero program, the federation considers it non-negotiable that the World Cup final be played on Spanish soil. During the recent official visit to Madrid by representatives of the international body, president Rafael Louzán and his team delivered a firm message: no venue outside Spain is being considered for the final. The federation insists that this demand is a "red line," while maintaining the utmost respect for its joint bid partners. At the technical meetings held at the Bernabéu , the various Spanish bodies demonstrated that the Madrid stadium meets all the requirements. The security plans, infrastructure and funding all dispelled the initial doubts raised by the international inspectors. However, FIFA still has certain reservations about local regulations, taxes and current legislation in some candidate cities. World football's governing body warned that it could drop already selected host venues if administrative obstacles persist. Meanwhile, this situation creates a significant opportunity for Valencia and Vigo, with the Mestalla stadium standing a strong chance of making the final list. The final decision on host venues will be announced before next summer, although the choice of venue for the final could be delayed until late 2027. item.title: Numbers behind Real Madrid superstar’s sensational performance despite international defeat
item.description: Numbers behind Real Madrid superstar’s sensational performance despite international defeat Real Madrid have witnessed the remarkable development of Arda Guler under Jose Mourinho this season. The Turkish international has increasingly established himself as one of the team’s most influential attacking players. The 21-year-old carried that confidence into the international break, producing an extraordinary individual performance against Belgium on Thursday. However, despite his efforts, Turkey suffered a disappointing 2-1 defeat in the UEFA Nations League. Guler produces a remarkable all-round display The Madrid youngster opened the scoring in the 20th minute with a sensational free-kick , leaving Belgian goalkeeper Senne Lammens with no chance. However, Belgium responded through Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere, scoring twice within three minutes to overturn the deficit. Guler’s performance was nothing short of exceptional: he registered 86 touches, completed 50 of his 55 passes and created one big chance, while all three of his attempted shots were on target. His shooting statistics were particularly impressive, generating 1.02 expected goals on target from opportunities worth just 0.24 xG. Guler also won 10 of his 14 duels and completed all three defensive tackles, demonstrating his willingness to contribute without possession. A performance that will encourage Mourinho The youngster’s display offered another reminder of why Mourinho has granted him greater positional freedom at Real Madrid. His ability to dictate possession, create opportunities and threaten the opposition goal makes him considerably more than a traditional attacking midfielder. Mourinho has already hinted that he sees Guler evolving into a No. 6 later in his career. The manager has also used him in a deeper midfield role at times. For now, though, Guler has found a home on the right wing for Los Blancos , and he seems to be getting better with every passing game. However, the absence of Vinicius Jr. through suspension meant Mourinho had no problem giving both Guler and Diomande regular minutes. item.title: Giants’ Jameis Winston reveals reason for comical cadence on 4th-down hard count
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Giants’ Jameis Winston reveals reason for comical cadence on 4th-down hard count appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jameis Winston fell behind J.J. McCarthy on the New York Giants ’ depth chart and is unlikely to ever be a full-time NFL starting quarterback again, but he still takes the field when called upon and performs his job with gusto. The perennially amped-up quarterback showed off his big personality during Thursday’s home game versus the Washington Commanders . Leading 21-17 with less than four minutes remaining, and facing fourth-and-1 on their own 11-yard line, the Giants tried their darndest to get their opponent to jump off sides. Winston exhausted all other options on the hard count before digging deep into his bag of tricks and asking the Commanders an incredibly important question . “Who let the dogs out,” he yelled with about five seconds left on the play clock. “Roof, Roof, Roof.” Players were obviously confused, but Washington did not bite. Following the unsuccessful yet amusing attempt to move the chains, there is another important question that needs to be asked. Why did Winston break out the Baha Men at this juncture? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It just had a nice ring to it,” the former Pro Bowler and No. 1 overall pick said after New York’s gut-wrenching 27-24 loss , per The Athletic’s Charlotte Carroll. Winston conceived the idea at practice, hoping that the phrase could rattle the defensive line. Some people will argue that Winston completely tipped the Giants’ hand and went way over the top, but perhaps they should look at the situation another way. Since the Commanders likely let their guard down after the man started barking, New York might have been able to steal a first down with a surprise QB run and significantly increase its chances of victory. Something to consider in the future maybe. Considering that the G-Men stumbled on offense down the stretch and missed key tackles, blowing what should have been their third divisional win of the season, fans could use a reason to smile and laugh. Jameis Winston delivered on that front and injected some fun in what was otherwise a disappointing night of football. item.title: ‘I want to play every game’ – Emotional Raphinha talks Barcelona, Brazil and surgery decision
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Raphinha of FC Barcelona looks on during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between Atletico de Madrid and FC Barcelona at Riyadh Air Metropolitano on November 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barcelona captain Raphinha has been on media duty ahead of Brazil’s friendlies against Japan and Singapore and has opened up on his game time and recent decision to undergo surgery. Raphinha says he wants to play as much as possible for club and country and was a little emotional at times. He also explained his recent decision to bring forward surgery for an ear cyst so that he would be available for Brazil. The Barcelona star revealed the procedure was just: “a small operation on the ear, nothing special or serious, to be able to be here.” Raphinha went on to talk about just how important it is for him to play for the national team. “From the first time I wore the national team jersey, I’ve always made it very clear that I wanted to be here. I never gave up on the national team, I always did everything in my power. It has always been an honor, a privilege, and nothing will change,” he added. “It’s the greatest national team in the world, I have no doubt, and we carry the weight of an entire nation wanting to see the national team winning and playing well. When the results don’t happen, we have to be held accountable for it.” The forward also spoke about his recent injuries and recent comments about his game time that caused some controversy back in Brazil. “Taking into account everything I’ve been through in the last three call-ups, with three injuries in practically the same area of my leg, what I meant was, simply, that I had to take care of myself. Obviously, I don’t want to get injured again. I want to be available not only for the national team, but also for Barcelona,” he added. “When you’re on the pitch you don’t think about the discomfort, you want to give your best. I always give 100%. Many times doctors and physiotherapists ask me to calm down, but I can’t change my style of play. “I want to play every game and as many minutes as possible. I also said that, if my body allows, I will give my best.” Raphinha also spoke about the conversation he had with Carlo Ancelotti about game time after he picked up an injury and returned early. “There was nothing out of the ordinary in our conversation. It was a normal conversation after what happened during the last FIFA international break, a super informal conversation about taking care of ourselves and being 100% fit, regardless of the number of minutes on the field. “I’m coming back from injury, I played a few games for Barcelona and only played the full 90 minutes in the last one.” The Barcelona captain is expected to skipper Brazil on Saturday when they play Japan in their first friendly of the break.
